picked.t: Vietnam's visa-free policy for Chinese tour groups strengthens its edge in Southeast Asia's tourism race
picked.body: The government on Oct.12 allowed Chinese nationals traveling in groups of two or more to visit Khanh Hoa Province, home to beach city Nha Trang, visa-free under a scheme lasting until Dec. 31, 2027, if they fly directly to Cam Ranh International Airport. Martin Koerner, commercial director of The Anam Group, which operates luxury resorts including one in Cam Ranh, described the move as "a positive step towards improving Vietnam's competitiveness in one of Asia's most important outbound tourism markets." Southeast Asian countries such as Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, and Cambodia already have visa-free entry for Chinese tourists, and report positive results. China is now the largest source of visitors for Thailand and Singapore, and Chinese arrivals to Malaysia last year increased by 25%. China is also Vietnam's largest international inbound market, with about 3.95 million arrivals in the first nine months of 2026, or 22.3% of all foreign visitors. For Khanh Hoa, the new policy could pave the way for more charter flights and organized tours, particularly from Chinese cities with strong demand for beach holidays, Koerner said. The resulting benefits could extend beyond hotels and resorts to restaurants, tourist attractions, transport operators, and other local businesses, he said. The Anam Cam Ranh Resort has experienced encouraging growth from the Chinese market over the past three years, he said. In 2025, Chinese guests generated 4,050 room nights, a 7.14% share. Dr Justin Matthew Pang, senior program manager for tourism and hospitality management at RMIT University Vietnam, said the move by the Vietnamese government is bold and strategic. "This promotion is a teaser to test what appeals to the Chinese tourist, especially in term of the mandatory tour package." Thai Thi Le Hang, director of the Khanh Hoa Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism, said China used to be a major inbound market for the province before the Covid pandemic, but its recovery since then has lagged behind South Korea and Russia. She said the pilot visa program would remove key procedural barriers, enabling travel agencies in both countries to develop and promote all-inclusive tour packages. Its value lies not only in the number of visitors it attracts but also in its potential to test market connectivity, tour operations, service delivery, and cooperation between businesses, she added. Industry insiders want the visa exemption to be extended to other localities if the Khanh Hoa attempt proves successful. "Expanding similar arrangements to destinations such as Da Nang and Lam Dong (home to Da Lat) could strengthen Vietnam's competitiveness in the leisure tourism market," Koerner said. Pang said: "Vietnam should not open the floodgates immediately. The case-study of Khanh Hoa must be thoroughly researched to ascertain the appeal factors, and limitations."

picked.t: Vietnam targets at least 10% GDP growth in 2027
picked.body: As the government expects 2027 to be a year of acceleration and breakthroughs, it also targets GDP per capita of $6,100, consumer price index growth at around 4.5%, and average labor productivity growth at 8.6%, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung told lawmakers at a meeting Saturday morning. The government also seeks breakthroughs in mobilizing, allocating and efficiently using all resources for development. It aims to increase budget revenue by 9.1% and curb recurrent spending. To diversify funding sources, the government plans to issue various types of bonds, secure official development assistance loans, mobilize credit and private resources, increase investment by state-owned enterprises and encourage foreign-invested companies to reinvest their profits in Vietnam. Hung pledged to continue managing interest rates and exchange rates appropriately. He said decisive and effective measures would be introduced to lower lending rates and direct credit toward production and business activities, exports, science and technology, and small and medium-sized enterprises. The government will also accelerate economic restructuring, renew the development model and strengthen the economy’s internal capacity, independence, self-reliance and resilience. It plans to expand the domestic industrial ecosystem, prioritizing foundational and supporting industries. Modern service and logistics hubs and special economic zones will be established. Reporting on the results for 2026, Hung said 14 of the 15 socioeconomic indicators were expected to meet or exceed their targets. GDP grew 9.95% in the third quarter and 9.01% in the first nine months, placing Vietnam among the fastest-growing economies in Southeast Asia and in the world. He said fiscal, monetary and other macroeconomic policies had been managed proactively and flexibly. Full-year budget revenue is estimated at VND3.06 quadrillion (US$118.2 billion), up 14%. Hung said the State Bank of Vietnam had directed credit institutions to jointly reduce lending rates by 1.5–2 percentage points for production and business activities and priority sectors, in line with directives from the Party’s central leadership and the government. Credit ratings agency Moody’s revised Vietnam’s sovereign credit outlook from "stable" to "positive" in May, while the stock market’s status was upgraded to Secondary Emerging Market in September. "International organizations have praised Vietnam’s resilience and growth prospects," the PM said. The government’s report also showed that industry and construction grew 11.21% in the first nine months, the highest rate since 2015. Foreign trade rose 30.4% and is estimated to reach $1.11 trillion for the full year, potentially surpassing the $1 trillion mark for the first time. Total investment across the economy reached VND3.11 quadrillion in the first nine months, up 15.1%. Public investment disbursement totaled nearly VND643 trillion, equivalent to 63% of the plan and almost 13% higher than a year earlier. Registered foreign direct investment reached $50.36 billion, up 76.4% and the highest level since 2021. On infrastructure, Vietnam completed another 395 kilometers of expressways and opened the entire eastern North-South Expressway to traffic. The government also took decisive steps to resolve problems affecting stalled and long-delayed projects. By the end of September, problems at 4,688 projects had either been resolved or had resolution plans in place. These projects cover nearly 196,000 hectares and have total investment exceeding VND3.2 quadrillion. The political and legal framework for fully resolving obstacles affecting wind power, solar power and mineral projects, among others, was also completed. For the remainder of the year, Hung said the government would "strive to achieve the best possible results, especially double-digit growth alongside macroeconomic stability and inflation control." The government will take decisive and effective measures to lower lending rates and ensure electricity and fuel supplies. "Localities must strive for the highest possible growth, especially the major growth hubs," he said. Presenting the appraisal report, Phan Van Mai, chairman of the National Assembly’s Economic and Financial Committee, said the committee commended the decisive and flexible leadership of the government and prime minister, as well as the efforts of ministries, agencies and localities. However, the committee highlighted six issues requiring the government’s attention in its management in the coming period. It said growth remained strong but rested on an uncertain foundation. Specifically, the four largest local economies – HCMC, Hanoi, Hai Phong and Dong Nai – which account for nearly 47% of gross regional domestic product, were all expected to miss their 2026 growth targets. picked.t: Vietnam's university admissions policies fuel costly IELTS race among high school students
picked.body: Thang, now a sophomore at a Hanoi university, said he enrolled in an IELTS preparation course when he was an 11th grader, aiming for a score of at least 6.0. The course cost VND55 million (US$2,090). On having him take the test twice and hiring private tutors for one-on-one lessons to improve his listening and speaking skills, his parents had spent more than VND100 million, despite being far from wealthy. Eventually, he got an IELTS score of 6.5 on his second attempt, allowing him to convert it into a perfect 10 in English. He was also offered 2.5 bonus points, which was added directly to his total university admission score for holding an international certificate. As a result, he could get into a mid-tier university. Students can get into university based on national high school graduation scores. High school students take four subjects for graduation: math, literature, and two electives from among a list of subjects including foreign language, history, physics, chemistry, biology, geography, economics and law education, information technology, and technology. For admission, universities use the aggregate scores of three subjects out of a maximum of 30 points, high school academic records, international English certificates such as IELTS, or a combination of these. Thang took the national high school graduation examination in the summer of 2025, and scored only 5.25 out of 10 in English. That year, the English test was widely considered to be "difficult." "Without the IELTS certificate, I might have had to attend a lower-rated university or even retake the entrance exam," he said. His experience reflects a pattern among tens of thousands of high school students in recent years as they recognize the advantage of an English proficiency certificate in getting university admission. Quan, now a 10th grader in Ho Chi Minh City, has yet to decide which university or major to pursue but already persuaded his parents to pay more than VND30 million for a course guaranteeing an IELTS score of 7.0, reasoning that it would be beneficial regardless of his future plans. Ngoc Hoai, a 12th grader in the northern Phu Tho Province, spent a similar amount and scored 5.5. She is preparing to retake the test, hoping to raise it to 6.5. "The certificate can be converted into a score of 9 or 10 in English at many universities," she said, adding that achieving comparable marks in the graduation exam would be much more challenging. The trend began in 2015, when the Ministry of Education and Training allowed students with recognized foreign language certificates to be exempt from the corresponding subject in the high school graduation exam and use their certificates for score conversion in graduation assessment. Two years later, the National Economics University (NEU) in Hanoi became the first to use such certificates for admissions. These days, more than 100 universities allow converting IELTS scores into English marks, award bonus points, or incorporate the certificate into combined admission schemes. Many institutions convert IELTS scores of 5.0 or higher, or equivalent qualifications, into English marks of 7-10. Additionally, students are given bonus points added to their total admission score if they have international language certificates (such as IELTS or TOEFL). The conversion scales are decided differently by each university. Others previously awarded up to three bonus points toward admission scores, before the ministry required the maximum to be reduced to 1.5 for this year. The number of IELTS certificate holders applying to universities has skyrocketed over the years. At NEU, applications with IELTS certificates rose from 50 in 2017 to 22,000-23,000 annually in the last two to three years. Between 2020 and 2026, the number increased 73-fold at the University of Economics and Law under the Vietnam National University, Ho Chi Minh City, and sevenfold at the Vietnamese-German University in the former Binh Duong Province. Data from the Education Ministry shows out of 1.24 million candidates who took the high school graduation exam this year, 874,811 registered for university admissions. Over 37,300 used English certificates to gain bonus points, with more than 35,900 using IELTS scores. "When the admissions benefits are substantial enough, the market inevitably responds, creating a race for certificates Dang Thi Ngoc Quyen, a senior manager at the British University Vietnam, said. "This is also why many intensive IELTS preparation centers have emerged." The British Council and IDP, the two organizations administering IELTS in Vietnam, do not publish annual candidate numbers, but the latter’s annual reports for 2023 and 2024 identified Vietnam as one of the world's three fastest-growing markets for the test. The IELTS training network has also expanded, encompassing language centers, high schools, universities, and education companies. picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City metro line stops running for 1 hour after power outage
picked.body: The incident began at around 7:04 a.m., when the entire 220 kV Thu Duc substation lost power due to a fault in the national power transmission system. Trains operating at the time were directed to the nearest stations, where passengers were asked to disembark and wait for services to resume. According to HURC1, the line’s operator, the power outage affected 14 trains. Services resumed at 7:57 a.m., after the power system was fixed and the company worked with the Southern Power System Dispatch Center to restore the supply. A HURC1 representative said the electricity system supporting metro operations depends on the national power grid. The incident marked the first time the Ben Thanh–Suoi Tien line had experienced a service disruption caused by a power failure originating from the grid. Since beginning commercial operations in December 2024, the line has experienced several disruptions caused by lightning strikes, which triggered electrical protection systems, forcing trains to stop as a safety precaution. The most recent incident occurred on Oct. 7, when a lightning strike near Tan Cang Station disrupted services for approximately four minutes. Disruptions due to power outages have happened to metro systems worldwide. In August 2025, Japan’s Osaka metro suspended services across the entire Chuo Line following a power supply problem. Some sections resumed operations overnight, but full service was not restored until the following morning, affecting the travel plans of tens of thousands of passengers. The Ben Thanh–Suoi Tien, HCMC's only running metro line, stretches nearly 20 km, comprising three underground stations and 11 elevated stations. It connects the city center with its eastern part. The line uses 17 trains, each consisting of three carriages. In its first year of operation, the metro line served approximately 19 million passenger trips, averaging 52,000 trips per day. By March 2026, daily ridership had risen to around 70,000 passenger trips.

picked.t: Hidden spy chip turns up in crypto wallet bought in Singapore, triggers investigation across 7 Asian markets
picked.body: Ben Yorke of crypto platform WOO said he bought the device, a Ledger Flex, from a Metapod store at Changi in June, Gizmodo reported. He never plugged it in and, after noticing scratches on the casing, sent it to Karpelès. Ledger has not confirmed the finding. Paris-based Ledger has asked resellers in seven Asian markets to pull its crypto hardware wallets from shelves after spy implants were found inside devices sold in the region, Bleeping Computer reported. The Oct. 13 request, which also covers distributors, applies in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong while the company investigates. Ledger said "the only confirmed incidents remain contained to Southeast Asia," that it had not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere, and that it had no sign its own systems or direct sales channel had been compromised. A hardware wallet stores the private keys to a user's cryptocurrency offline, out of reach of online hackers. Ledger opened its investigation on Oct. 9 after users reported stolen funds. All confirmed losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, a Malaysia-based reseller, and Ledger confirmed on Oct. 10 that one affected user's device contained an unauthorized hardware implant. CryptoBilis has stopped selling Ledger devices while the investigation continues, the company said. According to Ledger's security team, Donjon, the implant sits inside the casing and reads what appears on the screen. When the wallet displays its 24-word recovery phrase during setup, a microcontroller decodes the words and sends them out over a mobile network using an eSIM. Anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and move its funds. Because the implant leaves the device's secure chip and software untouched, Ledger's own "Genuine Check" tool cannot detect it, The Hacker News reported. The outlet said researchers at Tibane Labs have documented three versions of the implant, the most advanced of which was bought on Amazon Japan from a China-based seller and shipped from Malaysia. Pseudonymous blockchain investigator Specter estimated that more than $86 million had been stolen, and analytics firm Bitquery has since traced $102 million drained from 324 wallets across six blockchains. Ledger said it had not confirmed the number of affected users or the total lost, and that figures circulating online came from third parties. Besides the Changi device, a second tampered Ledger was reportedly bought from a Challenger store at VivoCity mall in Singapore, according to The Straits Times . Ledger, which began selling through Challenger's VivoCity and Bugis stores in March, has not said whether the Singapore devices are linked to the CryptoBilis cases. It said it is reviewing reports of implants in other devices and locations. In Europe, electronics retailer MediaMarktSaturn stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online on Oct. 13 after a customer in Germany reported an implant, Ledger said. On Oct. 14, Ledger said its team had inspected devices from retail and distributor stock across Germany, including units from the stores named in the reports, and found no sign of tampering. No loss of funds linked to implants has been reported anywhere in Europe, it said. Ledger's devices are made and assembled in France, Hungary and Vietnam, according to its website. Ledger has told anyone who bought a device from CryptoBilis not to set it up, and those who already have to move their assets to a new device with a new recovery phrase.

picked.t: Vietnam Mobility Show 2026 set for early December in Hanoi
picked.body: Following the 2025 event, which drew 60,000 visitors and featured more than 20 auto, motorbike, and accessory brands, the Vietnam Mobility Show (VnMS) organized by VnExpress returns to the Vietnam Exhibition Center in Hanoi's suburban Dong Anh District from Dec. 5–6 with an expanded slate of interactive attractions. At the center of the exhibition floor, automakers and motorcycle brands will spotlight green technology and sustainable transportation. Besides legacy manufacturers long established in the country, this year's expo will also see the debut of several homegrown brands. The hands-on test-drive pavilion promises to draw equal interest. Automakers are preparing nearly 100 of their latest models for visitors to put through their paces, navigating both dedicated obstacle courses designed by professional driving instructors and real-world open roads. The biggest crowd-puller for visitors of all ages will likely be the motorsports arena with around 300 sports cars, supercars, and custom builds from local owners besides dozens of imported machines. Professional drivers will run back-to-back car drifting and motorcycle stunt exhibitions in this zone throughout the weekend. Positioned as an engaging weekend outing for families rather than a conventional trade expo, the event includes the Carlympic Family Run, interactive road-safety educational playgrounds for children, and a diverse lineup of food vendors. The main stage will host interactive lifestyle seminars and life-skills workshops meant for visitors of all generations. For drivers seeking to personalize their vehicles, the aftermarket and accessories pavilion will feature new product launches alongside show-exclusive discounts. Coming just ahead of the peak Lunar New Year shopping season, the expo allows buyers to evaluate models on the showroom floor and behind the wheel before making a purchase. Automakers are also preparing promotional discounts and financing packages exclusive to ticket holders at the venue.

picked.t: IPP Travel Retail opens Travel Essentials store at Cam Ranh airport
picked.body: IPP Travel Retail opened its Travel Essentials store at Cam Ranh International Airport's international terminal on Sept. 30, combining practical travel products with locally inspired gifts and souvenirs. Cam Ranh serves Nha Trang and Khanh Hoa Province, connecting Vietnam's south-central coast with international markets. In 2025, the airport handled nearly 7.3 million passengers, including about 4.7 million international travelers. More than 30 airlines operate at the airport, which added 13 airlines and 14 routes in 2025, including connections to Seoul, Busan and Chengdu. The opening ceremony was attended by representatives of Cam Ranh International Terminal, airport authorities, partner brands and IPP Travel Retail. Phillip Nguyen, Vice President of IPPG and CEO of IPP Travel Retail, said the store aims to meet travelers' immediate needs while introducing Vietnamese culture to international visitors. "Every passenger who passes through here is an opportunity for us to introduce Vietnam to friends from around the world," he said. Travel Essentials features three main product categories: Travel Tech, offering electronic devices and accessories; Kids Toys & Hobbies, catering to children and families; and Local Gifts, featuring souvenirs and regional specialties. "We wanted more than just a convenience store. We wanted to understand what travelers need for their trip and help them take a little piece of Vietnam with them when they leave, through local gifts and our little friend TIPPI," Nguyen said. The store also introduced TIPPI, a mascot designed to represent the brand and its connection to Vietnamese culture. TIPPI features a rounded, cloud-like shape and friendly expression, wearing a traditional Vietnamese conical hat ( non la ) decorated with the national flag and an ao ba ba , a garment associated with southern Vietnam.
